requirement: The `habeas-requirements` skill MUST tell agents that the requirements commit may fail validation until evidence is authored, and that only the pull request as a whole must pass.
rationale:
The requirement has one obligation. The `habeas-requirements` skill must tell agents two things: the requirements commit may fail validation until evidence is authored, and only the pull request as a whole must pass.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_requirements_skill_expects_the_requirements_commit_to_fail_validation]` carries the `{test}` reference for this requirement. It calls `assert_phrases("habeas-requirements", ...)`. That helper builds the bundled skill text from `SKILL.md` plus its reference files, with whitespace collapsed, in `fn[bundled_skill]`. Then `fn[assert_text]` asserts that the text contains each phrase and panics with the skill name and phrase if one is missing.

The phrase is "This commit fails validation until evidence is authored; that is expected, as only the pull request as a whole must pass". It covers both halves of the obligation: failing validation until evidence is authored, and only the whole pull request needing to pass. The assertion is also scoped to the `habeas-requirements` skill, which is the skill the requirement names.

For a requirement about skill guidance text, checking that the exact phrase is present is the natural way to verify it. I found no other input classes, modes or boundaries in the requirement. The test does not assert every word of the requirement, and it doesn't need to. The one phrase states both halves, and removing or changing it would fail the test.

text: The `habeas-requirements` skill MUST tell agents that the requirements commit may fail validation until evidence is authored, and that only the pull request as a whole must pass.
